summary: Selective ARP-proxying on customer WAN causes egress MAC flapping, TLS session misbinding and gRPC connection fanout
description:
Issue summary: Since 2026-03-11 22:00 UTC EdgeFin has observed intermittent 5xxs and streaming stalls on their private deployment. The errors are most visible on high-concurrency chat endpoints and long-lived gRPC streams that rely on TLS session resumption. Impact: ~12% of requests during nightly batch windows see TLS resume failures or duplicate responses leading to downstream de-dup and timeouts. This is affecting production inference jobs and a subset of CI e2e tests.

Environment: Private VPC connected to EdgeFin corporate WAN via TGW peering + SD-WAN appliance. Redwood nodes run in customer's VPC behind VPCE with NAT through their egress appliances. Observed windows correspond to customer batch job schedules and SD-WAN path churn.

Steps to reproduce: 1) Run concurrent 200 client connections to /v1/chat/stream using same model and payload pattern. 2) Trigger an egress path switch on the SD-WAN (customer-side test tool). 3) Observe intermittent TLS session resume failures, occasional duplicate chunked responses and sudden gRPC fanout where a single request spawns multiple server-side handlers.

Observed logs/snippets: tcpdump on serving-node: "... ARP reply with same MAC for two different ENIs ..." conntrack dump: "... NAT mapping rebind ephemeral port 45678 -> 198.51.100.23:52345 then immediately 45678 -> 198.51.100.24:52345 ..." app logs: "tls: session ticket presented but peer IP mismatches, rejecting resume" gateway flowlog: "multiple src_mac changes within 60s for same src_ip"

Immediate customer-visible workaround: Ask customer to pause SD-WAN failover during nightly batch window and enable sticky SNAT (preserve source port) on their egress appliance. Temporary mitigation performed: customer applied sticky SNAT and error rate dropped to ~1.5% during a 2-hour window.
comments: 2026-03-12 15:10 UTC - Aisha Menon: Initial triage completed, collected tcpdumps and conntrack snapshots; escalated to Networking SRE.

2026-03-12 18:02 UTC - Marco Ortega: Reproduced locally with traffic generator; ARP proxying on the simulated SD-WAN caused MAC flip for the same source IP, leading to ephemeral port rebinds in conntrack.
2026-03-13 02:30 UTC - EdgeFin (Sara Liu): We've scheduled a controlled SD-WAN cutover for 2026-03-13 04:00 UTC and will leave sticky SNAT enabled. Noted improvement during earlier test window.

2026-03-14 09:20 UTC - Marco Ortega: Filed infra PR to add server-side stricter session-ticket validation and additional logging for mismatched src_mac events (see github.com/redwood/infra/pull/4123).
investigation_notes: Hypothesis: corporate SD-WAN appliance is acting as an ARP proxy/bridge and, under certain path-churn conditions, returns inconsistent src_mac for the same src_ip. This causes connection tracking (conntrack) entries to be re-associated with a different backend ENI and ephemeral port, creating 5-tuple collisions and TLS session reuse/misbinding on server side.

Evidence: multiple independent tcpdumps show same src_ip advertised with two distinct src_mac values within short intervals; conntrack logs show ephemeral port rebinds; server TLS stacks log session ticket origin mismatch.

Why gRPC fanout: when the 5-tuple changes mid-session the load-balancer/serving runtime sometimes re-establishes parallel streams which the application interprets as duplicated requests leading to multiple handlers processing the same logical request.
Repro: Traffic generator + SD-WAN path glitch reproduced locally; toggling ARP proxy off on appliance eliminates the behavior.
Workaround validated: enabling sticky SNAT on egress appliance keeps source port mappings stable and prevents conntrack rebinds; temporarily acceptable for EdgeFin's batch windows.
Risk: some customer networks cannot disable ARP proxying or change SNAT behavior; need long-term mitigations on both infra and runtime sides.

Next steps: collaborate with EdgeFin networking team to schedule a config change; implement server-side detection and reject suspicious resume attempts with better telemetry for postmortem; consider enqueuing a change to L7 load-balancer to key by connection-id as fallback.
resolution: Workaround applied: EdgeFin enabled sticky SNAT during nightly batches and paused SD-WAN failovers — errors reduced to baseline. Planned fixes: (1) infra PR to add extra logging and stricter TLS session-ticket origin checks (merged to staging, PR referenced above), (2) recommend permanent customer egress change to avoid ARP-proxying or to use a NAT gateway with persistent IPs/ports, (3) engineering follow-up to evaluate L7 keying fallback for long-lived streams. Postmortem to be created after full verification and customer config roll.
